correctness.rationale: The derivation identities were reconstructed from the Leibniz rule. Edge-square equations force every non-leaf column to be diagonal and impose factor-2 scaling along each edge; mixed-product equations leave only sink targets from leaf columns and weighted skew maps among sibling leaves. These subspaces are checked under commutators, giving the semidirect decomposition. In characteristic zero the weighted orthogonal factors of dimension at least three are semisimple, yielding the stated Levi factor. The packaged checker independently verifies the dimension formula on all 892 labeled no-isolated acyclic partial functional graphs on 2 through 5 vertices using two modular rank computations.

value.rationale: The result converts a broad weighted algebraic derivation problem into explicit rooted-forest data, gives an exact dimension formula, and exposes a sharp structural transition: three sibling leaves create a semisimple orthogonal Levi factor. This is more than a routine count; it identifies when derivations of a nilpotent evolution algebra cease to be solvable and supplies an explicit decomposition usable in symmetry and classification questions.
